Definition: Adonikam, the name of one or two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Adonikam is the head of a family that returned from exile — 666 of his sons in Ezra's list — and some of his later sons, Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, came up with Ezra, sixty males in all. His name appears again among those who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's day.
TheologicalSignificance: No doctrine hides in this name, and I won't look for one. What it keeps is the scale of the return — hundreds in one family alone — and the fact that the same families who came home also put their names to the covenant.
RelatedTopics: Exile and Return; Return from exile; Covenant renewal
